_about: Hand check and labels for run (e4): the S4d + S4e system on development set 4, first try. Written after reading every reply, before any fix. The marker's score is the official one.

D4-M02.why: The two renewals are listed under 'To receive' with 'Total to receive', and the lead says 'To receive … you should renew'. They are payments. The hybrid reader let Qwen choose the kind ('renews' is not a bill word), and it chose 'money owed to you'.

D4-M07.why: Right content (electricity bill on the 18th, Divya's exams running). It failed because the exam range is listed once per day, and the marker does not count days inside a range as memory dates. The repetition is a code fault (see labels).

D4-M09.why: 'I have Revathi's son Kiran (4 to 5 April), but nothing about wedding': the item is the wedding ('getting married'). The answer contradicts itself.

D4-P15.why: 'You told me Tara is your cousin. You haven't told me more than that.' is right and not self-contradictory; the marker's consistency rule caught 'haven't told me'.

D4-M02: 'Renews' (subscriptions) is not a bill word, so Qwen chose the kind and chose 'receivable'.
D4-M04: 'By when does the GSTR-1 have to be filed?' was read as a period ('today'), so a window list said 'Nothing saved on Monday 8 March'.
D4-M05: 'Anything due …' was read as payments and money only; the task also wanted the surgery (not 'due'). Kept as a failure.
D4-M07: A range item (exams 15–30 March) is repeated on every day of the window instead of listed once.
D4-M09: 'wedding' does not match 'getting married' (no related-word matching), so a partial-match answer was given for the right item.
D4-M13: 'before the engagement' did not find 'getting engaged on 27 March' (engagement vs engaged), so no period; it then went to status and said nothing was saved.
D4-P13: Own name resolved correctly ('my dentist appointment'), but 'appointment' is treated as a key term and the saved sentence says 'Dentist Dr. Shetty…', so a partial-match answer was given.
D4-P15: Consistency rule false positive on 'haven't told me more than that'.
D4-F04: Qwen gave [100000, 8, 2, 1]; the 1 ('compounded yearly', as the prompt says) is not in the question, so it was refused.
D4-F08: 'How many weeks from … to …' is not a maths phrase; it went to general knowledge and Qwen said 52 weeks.
D4-F09: Qwen added conversion factors to the numbers; code needs only the 5.
D4-F10: '1.2 crore in lakh' went to general knowledge (right answer, no working, label General answer).
D4-F11: 'Write ₹45,00,000 in lakh' went to writing ('Write…'), and Qwen said 4.5 lakh (wrong).
D4-F14: Qwen chose the wrong formula, but its expression '1240 + 860 + 499' was right; code did not fall back to the valid expression.
D4-F15: Same as F09: extra numbers for the °F → °C conversion.
D4-K07: 'Vikram Sarabhai' (it is A. P. J. Abdul Kalam).

route_mismatches: D4-M04 window (lookup expected), D4-M13 status (window expected), D4-F02 and D4-F03 mixed (maths expected; 'What do I pay' is personal; answers right), D4-F08 general, D4-F10 general, D4-F11 writing
other_findings: People and profile: 13/15 by the marker, 14/15 by hand. Reverse relationships, Indian terms, the own-name rewrite and the gender-neutral cousin answer all worked on first try.
Glossary: all 5 Indian-term questions right (run (e3) had 'UPI = United Parcel Service').
All 3 general-knowledge failures are Qwen 1.5B facts (Missile Man, national animal, 212°F).
Maths: every fallback was a correct choice of formula or expression rejected by my checks; no wrong number was shown.
